sentences.text: Three ranges describe how far a light can be seen.
Nominal range is the distance a light carries in clear weather, defined as a meteorological visibility of ten nautical miles.
That’s the number on the chart and in the Light List.
Luminous range is how far the light carries in the visibility actually present tonight, which you find with the luminous range diagram in the Light List.
Geographic range is how far you could see the light before the curve of the earth hides it, which depends on the light’s height and your height of eye.
The distance at which you’ll actually first see the light is the lesser of the luminous range and the geographic range.
